`experimental.evidence_binding`, keyed like `policy.yaml` (`case`,

FamilySurface.description:
One artifact family (the files under `spec/`: ledger, divergences,

recordKinds.description: The record kinds (as `--kind` names them) whose wire name is this family's.

schema.description: The family's JSON Schema, next to the record kinds' schemas.

KindSurface.description:
One record kind's authoring shape: the fields an agent must supply, the
partition it lands in, and its current schema version.

envelopeFields.description:
Every top-level field name this kind's record carries (envelope
fields `schema`/`kind`/`at`/`actor` flattened alongside the kind's
own business fields — `#[serde(flatten)]` puts them all in the same
JSON object, so "envelope fields" for authoring purposes means the
whole top-level shape) mapped to whether it is required.

schema.description: The kind's JSON Schema, relative to the repository root of canon itself.

schemaVersion.description:
This kind's CURRENT format generation, read straight from
[`canon_model::RecordKind::schema_version`] — never a
hand-maintained copy, so `canon context` can never advertise a
generation no writer stamps (`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`).

Literal.description:
A record field's literal value (plugin §7 lineage, from the donor manifest

YAML value against a declared [`Type`]. `Map` carries `evidence`'s
`{kind, ref}` structure (and any other future record-shaped attr).

PartitionLayout.description:
The Hive-style partition layout one record kind's git-tier files follow —

PolicyFieldSurface.description:

policy shape, matching invariant 1's "describes what CAN be authored").

PolicySurface.description:
`canon_gate::PolicyResolution`'s own fields, summarized field-by-field
via [`PolicyFieldSurface`] — one Rust field per `PolicyResolution` field,

`PolicyResolution::is_clean()` — whether `policy.yaml` loaded with

diagnostics.description:
`PolicyDiagnostic::to_string()` per problem `resolve()` recorded,
in the order `resolve()` encountered them (deterministic per repo
state, matching invariant 3 — this is never sorted, since it is
already reproducible byte-for-byte on an unchanged repo).

spec_coverage.description:
s44's opt-in spec-corpus requirement. `None` (JSON `null`) = the

Actor.description:
Who/what produced a record — structured, never a bare `by: String`
(design D2, the donor audit's biggest cross-family gap).

`role` is `Option` (S11 design D5, "actor backfill is best-effort
from adjacent fields; absent stays absent"): a migrated legacy
record whose only source field is a bare `by: "legacy-ci-machine"`
string carries no role information at all — `canon migrate` maps
that string to `agent_id` and leaves `role: null` rather than
guessing, so the field must be able to express "unknown", not just
"known". Every record canon itself originates still supplies a role
via [`Actor::new`]; only backfilled/migrated records use
[`Actor::new_unattributed`].

Change.description:
A change: the top of the join spine's `change_id` row (change ↔
tasks ↔ specs). `subject_ids` links an imported plan change to every
durable [`Subject`] it was adopted under (0.18 D4: a change may belong
to several subjects; per-task subjects are out of scope). It is a
plain `pub` field left empty by [`Change::new`] and appended to by
`canon-cli`'s `subject adopt` at adoption time (mirroring how
[`Session::project_key`] is set outside this crate), never derived
here. Skipped when empty, so an unadopted change carries no key.

# Old records
The ledger is append-only. A change written before 0.18 carries a
single `subject_id` string; it reads as a one-element `subject_ids`
([`one_or_many_subjects`]) and is never rewritten. Renaming the field
is a format generation change on a kind whose `at` can be byte-stable
(plan import), so [`RecordKind::Change`] is at schema `2`.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

ChangeId.description: openspec change slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the directory name under `openspec/changes/` — joins: change ↔ tasks ↔ specs

ChangeStatus.description:
A `Change`'s lifecycle state (mirrors an openspec change's own
proposal → tasks → archive flow).

MalformedEntry.description:
One structurally-broken construct a [`PlanAdapter::parse`] call
skipped (s18 `loud-plan-import-diagnostics` spec's "Every malformed
plan-import construct is named by path and reason"): a NAMED entry
carrying the construct's relative path and a reason drawn from a
fixed, per-adapter reason vocabulary — never an anonymous increment
to a bare count with no way to identify WHICH construct failed or
WHY. `hint` carries an additional actionable hint for a specific
near-miss signature (e.g. the openspec dialect's root-one-level-
too-high `changes`-basename hint) — `None` for every ordinary
malformed entry.

hint.description:
An additional actionable hint for a specific near-miss
signature — `None` for every ordinary malformed entry.

path.description:
The construct's path (relative to the source root when
derivable — never an absolute path leaking the host filesystem
layout into a persisted/printed diagnostic).

reason.description:
A stable reason string drawn from the adapter's own fixed
vocabulary (e.g. the openspec dialect's `"missing-proposal-md"`,
`"invalid-change-id-grammar"`, `"unreadable-directory"`).

NonCleanSource.description:
One configured source this pass found `malformed > 0` AND persisted
ZERO records for (`changes_persisted == 0 && tasks_persisted == 0`)
— s18 `loud-plan-import-diagnostics` spec's "A malformed-nonzero,
zero-persisted source makes canon ingest plans non-clean at the
process level". Never flagged for a legitimately empty/fresh source
(`malformed == 0`) or a partial success (`persisted > 0`) — see
[`run`]'s own flagging logic.

PlanSourceSummary.description:
One configured source's contribution to a pass (human + `--json`
output, task 3.5: "per-source counts + drop diagnostics + malformed
tallies").

changesUnwritten.description:
Degraded to the `unwritten` seam (a routed tier unreachable/
unrouted) — the bodies themselves are in
[`PlansOutcome::unwritten_changes`]/`unwritten_tasks`.

cursorAdvanced.description:
`true` iff this source's watermark cursor was refreshed this
pass — `false` for a skipped-unchanged source (nothing to
refresh) AND for a (re-)parsed source with any unwritten
candidate (the pass was not fully durable).

duplicateChangeId.description:
`change_id`s this source lost to an EARLIER-configured source
this pass (design D8) — that `Change` and every `Task` under it
were skipped entirely, never persisted.

malformed.description:
Structurally-broken constructs the adapter itself skipped
(design D3) — distinct from `duplicate_change_id`, which this
driver (not the adapter) detects. Each one NAMED by path +
reason [+ hint] (s18 `loud-plan-import-diagnostics` spec) —
`.len()` is the scalar tally a caller that only needs the count
reaches for.

skippedUnchanged.description:
`true` iff the S3-generalized watermark gate skipped this
source wholesale (byte-identical to its cursor) — every other
field is `0`/empty in that case.

unmapped.description:
Per-construct NAMED unmapped-drop counts straight from the
adapter's [`PlanParseOutcome`] (design D3).

RecordKind.description:
The fourteen closed record kinds `canon-model` recognizes (design D1;
`Subject` is the reviewed 13th kind, added by s36, and `Finding` the
reviewed 14th, added by s43 — the "a new kind is a reviewed, breaking
`canon-model` change" process design D1 mandates, exercised twice for
real). A fifteenth kind is again a reviewed, breaking
change — never a `kind: String` escape hatch (design D1's explicitly
rejected alternative: an untyped `payload: serde_json::Value` would
silently recreate the "no documented join key" problem inside canon
itself).

RoleId.description: kebab-case role slug (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), e.g. `implementer`, `reviewer` — joins: not a join-spine key; used by `Actor.role` and `regime_key`'s `<role>` segment

ScenarioId.description: `<area>.<surface>.<nn>` — `[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z0-9-]+\.\d{2,}`; never renumbered once assigned — joins: spec ↔ test ↔ ledger ↔ divergence

SessionId.description: opaque, non-empty agent-CLI session token; derivation source varies by adapter (Claude Code/Codex: transcript filename stem; omp/pi: in-file header `id` field) — this type validates shape only, never a single fixed format — joins: session ↔ cost ↔ run ↔ trajectory

SubjectId.description: subject slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the durable product-unit identifier — joins: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario

Task.description:
A task within a change (join-spine `task_id` row: task ↔ evidence ↔
trajectory). `change_id` is never a separate field — `task_id`
already embeds it; use [`TaskId::change_id`] to decompose.

depends_on.description:
Optional, declaratively-authored DEPENDENCY references (s37
`execution-graph-topology`, subject `flywheel-execution-graph`)
— which sibling `Task`(s) in the SAME change this task's own
plan text declares it comes after. Populated ONLY from a
dependency expression the dialect's corpus demonstrably uses
(the openspec dialect's in-row `depends on <n>`/`after <n>`
marker prose; the superpowers dialect's `- Consumes: … from
Task <n>` interface line), never from a syntax invented for
canon's convenience and never from dotted-numbering nesting —
`<change>#6.2` does NOT implicitly depend on `<change>#6`. A
reference that fails to resolve to a real sibling row is
DROPPED with a named import diagnostic, never an import
failure, because prose is ambiguous and "malformed evidence is
no evidence".

DECLARED INTENT ONLY: canon never schedules, orders, blocks, or
executes anything from this field. It is the PLAN-side half of
the execution graph — the half s37's plan-vs-actual diff reads
against `Run.parent_run_id`'s OBSERVED dispatch lineage, which
is what makes a declared-but-never-honored ordering visible to
the reward flywheel at all.

Empty by default, mirroring [`Task::scenario_refs`]'s own
additive-field shape (and, like it, `skip_serializing_if` so an
empty vec never introduces a spurious key — every pre-s37
`Task` stays byte-identical on the wire, and its content digest
with it).

This field IS nonetheless what bumped `Task` to
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] `2`
(`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`), and NOT because the wire form
broke — it did not. A `Task`'s `Envelope.at` is
`file_modified_at(<source plan doc>)` (s20 D7), byte-stable so an
unchanged plan re-imports idempotently; adding this field changed
the PARSER, not the source document's mtime, so the stale and
fresh record for one `task_id` carry an IDENTICAL `at` and
`canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key` needs a generation signal
to order them. Without the bump it fell through to the
lexicographic digest tie-break and surfaced this field on an
arbitrary SUBSET of one file's rows. See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for why `Run`/`Handoff` gained
fields on the same branch and correctly stayed at `1`.

scenario_refs.description:
Optional, declaratively-authored scenario-coverage references
(design s20 Decision 1) — which `Scenario`(s) this task is
meant to satisfy, populated ONLY from an explicit `[covers:
…]` `tasks.md` segment, never inferred from prose. Empty by
default, mirroring `EvidenceRecord.surface_ref`'s own
additive-field shape; a `Task` with no declared refs is
byte-identical to a pre-s20 `Task` on the wire.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

TaskId.description: `<change_id>#<n>`, where `<n>` is one or more dot-separated integers (`1`, `1.1`, `6.2`) matching `tasks.md`'s own numbering — joins: task ↔ evidence ↔ trajectory

TaskStatus.description:
A `tasks.md` checkbox's canonical state — `Open` is the unchecked
`- [ ]`, `Done` the checked `- [x]`. `evidence_note` carries the
same "one-line evidence note" discipline this very change's own
tasks.md is held to — a `Done` task without one is a checkbox
overclaim, not evidence.

dryRun.description:
A `--dry-run` preview: nothing was persisted and no cursor moved;
the `*Persisted` counts are what a real pass would persist.

nonCleanSources.description:
Every source this pass flagged non-clean (s18 spec) — the CLI
layer (`main.rs::run_ingest_plans`) prints an unconditional
stderr WARN per entry and exits non-zero whenever this is
non-empty. Empty for an ordinary clean/partial-success pass.

unwrittenChanges.description:
Every `Change`/`Task` a routed-but-unreachable (or wholly
unrouted) tier could not accept this pass — printed, never
silently dropped, never fatal to a sibling record whose tier
write already succeeded (spec "An unreachable pg tier degrades
to the unwritten seam").

ArtifactAdapterSummary.description:
One registered adapter's contribution to this pass — mirrors
`crate::ingest::AdapterSummary`'s per-adapter shape, generalized
with a `status` field so a `Records`-source read failure is a
visible, distinct outcome (module doc's "documented seam"), never
collapsed into the same zero-events shape an unconfigured
`Path`-source adapter reports.

status.description:
`"read"` (this adapter's source was actually reached, whether
or not it was configured/had records) | `"unavailable"` (a
`Records`-source read failed before `parse` ever ran) |
`"disabled"` (a `native_verdict: true` entry, S15 P4, whose
`ArtifactSourceConfig::native_records` switch is off — never
`"unavailable"`, which is reserved for a genuine read failure).

ConvergenceConflict.description:
One superseded copy the raw convergence KEPT rather than deleted,
because it carries an independently-written field the canonical row
does not (module doc, "The derivation key is NOT enough to authorize
that delete"). s42 (`close-the-open-loops`) re-review, `ReviewRuns`
finding 1.

A report, never a resolution. Both rows stay exactly as they are, so
`canon strategy promote` keeps reading the contradiction off
`query_by_regime_key` — which is the whole point: the alternative
this replaced silently deleted the loser and changed what the gate
saw.

canonicalId.description:
The row the smallest-id rule keeps
([`canonical_driver_row`]) — the one whose provenance the kept
row was compared against.

claims.description:
Every claim `retained_id` makes that `canonical_id` does not,
one line per disagreeing field in [`RowProvenance`]'s fixed field
order ([`RowProvenance::claims_beyond`]). Never empty — an empty
list IS the deletable case, and no conflict is constructed for it.

regimeKey.description: The namespace both rows sit under.

retainedId.description:
The superseded row that survived the delete. Still withheld from
the distiller exactly as s41 left it: kept is not served.

PersistedTrajectory.description: One regime showed trajectory this pass persisted.

superseded.description:
`true` when this write REPLACED this driver's own earlier
derivation of the same logical verdict set in place
([`plan_trajectory`]) rather than appending a new row — the
upgrade path the module doc describes. Reported per row rather
than as a second top-level counter, so the tally
[`format_human`] prints can never desync from the rows it
describes.

convergenceConflicts.description:
Superseded copies this pass REFUSED to delete because they carry
a `verdict_record` or `run_id` the canonical row does not — s42
(`close-the-open-loops`) re-review (`ReviewRuns` finding 1). One
entry per kept row, ordered by regime key then by the kept row's
own id, so a repeat pass prints byte-identical lines.

Empty for every store this driver produced on its own, and for
every ordinary upgrade: the losing copies a pre-s38 pass appended
were never marked and never attributed, so they claim nothing.
A non-empty entry means two stored rows disagree about a fact
`canon strategy promote` reads (module doc), and the disagreement is
STANDING — it is re-reported every pass until an operator removes
the row they judge wrong, because this driver will not pick for
them.

dryRun.description:
A `--dry-run` preview: nothing was written; the counts are what a
real pass would do (convergence of superseded copies is not previewed).

strategyItemsRebuilt.description:
Sum of every regime's freshly-distilled `StrategyItem` count
([`NamespaceConvergence::items`]) — the count that actually lands
in `stg_strategy_items`, i.e. what makes S9's `mart_role_memory`
non-empty.

trajectoriesConvergedDeleted.description:
Raw `Trajectory` rows this pass DELETED as this driver's own
superseded copies whose independently-written provenance the
canonical row also carries ([`RawConvergence::deletable`]) — s42
(`close-the-open-loops`).

Reported rather than left silent, on the same "reported, never
silent" discipline every other degrade and skip in this outcome
follows. It is the only counter here that names bytes that no
longer exist, so an operator seeing it non-zero should read the
module doc's account of what a deleted row makes unresolvable. It
is non-zero at most ONCE per namespace per upgrade: a namespace a
post-s38 canon produced on its own has no superseded copies to
remove, and one converging pass empties an upgraded one of every
copy it is allowed to remove — the rest are reported in
[`ArtifactIngestOutcome::convergence_conflicts`] and never
counted here.

trajectoriesLeftPending.description:
Trajectories deliberately LEFT `Pending`: the role's own
`RewardFn` resolved to [`VerdictOutcome::Pending`], which
`mark_trajectory_verdict` rejects outright
([`canon_learn::LearnError::CannotMarkVerdictPending`]) because
`Pending` is the unset default, never a covering-verdict write.
The `dev` role reaches this legitimately: `compute_dev_reward`'s
additive triad stays `Pending` below a full `1.0` (a partial
`pr-merged` + `ci-pass` without `no-rollback`), waiting for the
S7 webhook receiver's no-rollback timer to resolve it. Counted,
never an error.

trajectoriesMarked.description:
Trajectories whose covering verdict+reward was RESOLVED and
written back in this same pass
([`canon_learn::RewardRegistry::compute_for_trajectory`] +
[`canon_learn::mark_trajectory_verdict`]). Every freshly
constructed `Trajectory` starts `VerdictOutcome::Pending` (S7
design D2's two-phase reward-write model), and S7's promotion
gates read `verdict_record.outcome`, NOT the raw `verdicts`
list — so a trajectory left `Pending` is invisible to
`OccurrencePromotionGate`/`CrnPromotionGate` and can never
corroborate a promotion. This counter is what makes the
artifact-ingest half of the flywheel observable.

trajectoriesSkippedDuplicate.description:
A trajectory whose FULL identity (identity-shape version +
`regime_key` + ordered `VerdictRow` contents + the rendered
`task`/`context`) already matches a trajectory this exact
`regime_key` holds ([`trajectory_content_digest`]) — skipped and
counted (module doc's write-time idempotence), never a
double-write of an unchanged corpus. A row whose verdict set
matches but whose TEXT does not is not this: it is superseded in
place, see [`PersistedTrajectory::superseded`].

trajectoriesSkippedUnregisteredRole.description:
A trajectory whose `regime_key` role is not registered in this
repo's `canon_learn::RoleRegistry` (`canon.yaml` `learn.roles`,
or the built-in set) — skipped and counted (module doc's
"documented seam"), never a fatal error for the rest of the
batch.

Actor.description:
Who/what produced a record — structured, never a bare `by: String`
(design D2, the donor audit's biggest cross-family gap).

`role` is `Option` (S11 design D5, "actor backfill is best-effort
from adjacent fields; absent stays absent"): a migrated legacy
record whose only source field is a bare `by: "legacy-ci-machine"`
string carries no role information at all — `canon migrate` maps
that string to `agent_id` and leaves `role: null` rather than
guessing, so the field must be able to express "unknown", not just
"known". Every record canon itself originates still supplies a role
via [`Actor::new`]; only backfilled/migrated records use
[`Actor::new_unattributed`].

ChangeId.description: openspec change slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the directory name under `openspec/changes/` — joins: change ↔ tasks ↔ specs

RecordKind.description:
The fourteen closed record kinds `canon-model` recognizes (design D1;
`Subject` is the reviewed 13th kind, added by s36, and `Finding` the
reviewed 14th, added by s43 — the "a new kind is a reviewed, breaking
`canon-model` change" process design D1 mandates, exercised twice for
real). A fifteenth kind is again a reviewed, breaking
change — never a `kind: String` escape hatch (design D1's explicitly
rejected alternative: an untyped `payload: serde_json::Value` would
silently recreate the "no documented join key" problem inside canon
itself).

Reopen.description: A recorded reopen of a shipped subject (see [`Subject::reopen`]).

change.description:
The approved change the follow-up work goes into: the subject's
newest adopted change when it reopened. Absent when it adopted
none.

RoleId.description: kebab-case role slug (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), e.g. `implementer`, `reviewer` — joins: not a join-spine key; used by `Actor.role` and `regime_key`'s `<role>` segment

SessionId.description: opaque, non-empty agent-CLI session token; derivation source varies by adapter (Claude Code/Codex: transcript filename stem; omp/pi: in-file header `id` field) — this type validates shape only, never a single fixed format — joins: session ↔ cost ↔ run ↔ trajectory

StatusOverride.description:
A recorded waiver of the `spec_coverage.require_review` status guard
(see [`Subject::status_override`]). `canon gate check` reports a gap
as an advisory naming this waiver only when it matches one of
`waived` exactly, and only while the subject stays at `to`. A gap that
appears later (a new blocker, a newly tagged scenario) is not covered
and stays a violation.

to.description: The status the transition moved to under this waiver.

waived.description: Exactly the guard violations this waiver let through, sorted.

Subject.description:
A subject (join-spine `subject_id` row: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario)
— the durable product/management unit a team plans, designs, builds,
and measures across many changes (s36, the reviewed 13th kind). A
by-id kind like [`Change`]: flat Hive partition, no mandatory
`scenario_id`. `domain` is a validated-shape-only kebab slug (see
[`deserialize_domain_slug`] — the closed vocabulary lives in
`canon/vocab`, not here); `owner_role` names the accountable role;
`change_ids` accumulates as plan changes are adopted
(additive-empty by default, so a freshly-authored subject with no
links yet is still a valid, minimal record). One change may be listed
by several subjects (0.18 D4); the change's own
[`Change::subject_ids`] lists each of them, and readers join a
subject to its changes from both sides.

The scenario side of the join lives on [`Scenario::subject_id`], set
by `canon inventory sync` from each scenario's `@subject:<id>` tag —
the spec corpus is the one place that link is authored. A subject
carries no copy of it: a second, separately-written list is exactly
what drifted (never populated, so every reader saw zero scenarios and
the ship gate passed on an empty set). Records written before that
list was removed still deserialize; the stale key is ignored.

reopen.description:
Who reopened this subject from `shipped` to `verifying`, and why
(0.18 D3, `canon subject status <id> --to verifying --reason`). Set
only on the record that reopens; every other `canon subject
status` write clears it, like [`Self::status_override`]. Skipped
when absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

status_override.description:
The accountable waiver this record's status transition was let
through under, when `spec_coverage.require_review` refused it and
the operator passed `canon subject status --override-reason`.
Skipped when absent, so every subject written without one stays
byte-identical on the wire. Each `canon subject status` write
clears it and sets it again only when it waives something, so a
waiver never outlives the status it was granted for.

status_reason.description:
The note an operator gave the transition that wrote this record
(`canon subject status <id> --to <state> --reason`, 0.21.1), on
any transition; a reopen records it here too, next to
[`Self::reopen`]. Every `canon subject status` write clears it
and sets it again only when given a `--reason`. Skipped when
absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

SubjectId.description: subject slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the durable product-unit identifier — joins: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario

SubjectStatus.description:
A `Subject`'s lifecycle (s36 design D1): the states a product unit
moves through, `proposed → specced → building → verifying → shipped
→ retired`. Transitions are policy-gated (CEL) at the CLI/gate layer
(s35 seam); this enum owns only the closed set and its stable
snake_case wire spelling.

WaivedViolation.description:
One violation a [`StatusOverride`] let through: the gate failure
class (`unreviewed-promotion`, `open-blocker`) and the violation's
subject (a scenario id, or `<change_id>#<round>.<seq>` for a
blocker), as `canon gate check` prints them.

SessionId.description: opaque, non-empty agent-CLI session token; derivation source varies by adapter (Claude Code/Codex: transcript filename stem; omp/pi: in-file header `id` field) — this type validates shape only, never a single fixed format — joins: session ↔ cost ↔ run ↔ trajectory

StatusOverride.description:
A recorded waiver of the `spec_coverage.require_review` status guard
(see [`Subject::status_override`]). `canon gate check` reports a gap
as an advisory naming this waiver only when it matches one of
`waived` exactly, and only while the subject stays at `to`. A gap that
appears later (a new blocker, a newly tagged scenario) is not covered
and stays a violation.

to.description: The status the transition moved to under this waiver.

waived.description: Exactly the guard violations this waiver let through, sorted.

Subject.description:
A subject (join-spine `subject_id` row: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario)
— the durable product/management unit a team plans, designs, builds,
and measures across many changes (s36, the reviewed 13th kind). A
by-id kind like [`Change`]: flat Hive partition, no mandatory
`scenario_id`. `domain` is a validated-shape-only kebab slug (see
[`deserialize_domain_slug`] — the closed vocabulary lives in
`canon/vocab`, not here); `owner_role` names the accountable role;
`change_ids` accumulates as plan changes are adopted
(additive-empty by default, so a freshly-authored subject with no
links yet is still a valid, minimal record). One change may be listed
by several subjects (0.18 D4); the change's own
[`Change::subject_ids`] lists each of them, and readers join a
subject to its changes from both sides.

The scenario side of the join lives on [`Scenario::subject_id`], set
by `canon inventory sync` from each scenario's `@subject:<id>` tag —
the spec corpus is the one place that link is authored. A subject
carries no copy of it: a second, separately-written list is exactly
what drifted (never populated, so every reader saw zero scenarios and
the ship gate passed on an empty set). Records written before that
list was removed still deserialize; the stale key is ignored.

reopen.description:
Who reopened this subject from `shipped` to `verifying`, and why
(0.18 D3, `canon subject status <id> --to verifying --reason`). Set
only on the record that reopens; every other `canon subject
status` write clears it, like [`Self::status_override`]. Skipped
when absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

status_override.description:
The accountable waiver this record's status transition was let
through under, when `spec_coverage.require_review` refused it and
the operator passed `canon subject status --override-reason`.
Skipped when absent, so every subject written without one stays
byte-identical on the wire. Each `canon subject status` write
clears it and sets it again only when it waives something, so a
waiver never outlives the status it was granted for.

status_reason.description:
The note an operator gave the transition that wrote this record
(`canon subject status <id> --to <state> --reason`, 0.21.1), on
any transition; a reopen records it here too, next to
[`Self::reopen`]. Every `canon subject status` write clears it
and sets it again only when given a `--reason`. Skipped when
absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

SubjectId.description: subject slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the durable product-unit identifier — joins: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario

SubjectStatus.description:
A `Subject`'s lifecycle (s36 design D1): the states a product unit
moves through, `proposed → specced → building → verifying → shipped
→ retired`. Transitions are policy-gated (CEL) at the CLI/gate layer
(s35 seam); this enum owns only the closed set and its stable
snake_case wire spelling.

WaivedViolation.description:
One violation a [`StatusOverride`] let through: the gate failure
class (`unreviewed-promotion`, `open-blocker`) and the violation's
subject (a scenario id, or `<change_id>#<round>.<seq>` for a
blocker), as `canon gate check` prints them.

SubjectUnadoptReport.description: `data` of the subject leaves: the Subject record, embedded verbatim (it keeps the ledger record's own schema and snake_case keys).
SubjectUnadoptReport.title: SubjectReport

TaskDoneReport.description: `canon task done`: the task row flipped, or already done.

document.description: The task document written; absent when nothing was flipped.

flipped.description: False when the row was already `[x]`.

TaskDoneReport.title: TaskDoneReport

Effect.description:
One thing a destructive run would do (or did): the `action`, and the file
(`path`, repo-relative) or record (`record`) it acts on.

detail.description: Where it goes, or why, when `action` alone does not say.

path.description: The file acted on, relative to the repo.

record.description: The record acted on (an id, key or digest) when it is not a file.

TierAgeRule.description: One `aging:` rule in `canon tier age`'s report.

TierAgeReport.description: `canon tier age`'s `data`: the plan and one entry per `aging:` rule.

committed.description: `true` once the run acted, `false` for a preview.

effects.description: Everything the run would do, in the order it does it.

planDigest.description: sha256 (hex) of the plan's `effects`; `--commit --plan-digest` must repeat it.
